records.source: וְהִתְנַבִּ֞י חַגַּ֣י נְבִיָּ֗א וּזְכַרְיָ֤ה בַר־עִדּוֹא֙ נְבִיַּיָּ֔א עַל־יְה֣וּדָיֵ֔א דִּ֥י בִיה֖וּד וּבִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם בְּשֻׁ֛ם אֱלָ֥הּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֲלֵיהֽוֹן׃ס
records.gloss: And prophesied Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, the prophets, to the Jews who [were] in Judah and in Jerusalem, in [the] name of [the] God of Israel [who was] over them.
pieces: Now the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.

L.1: And Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, the prophets, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and in Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel, [who was] over them.

R.1: Then two prophets, Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo, spoke God's messages to the Jews who lived in Judah and Jerusalem. They spoke in the name of the God of Israel, who ruled over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

decisions.choice: Haggai and Zechariah: the two prophets whose books stand in the Bible
decisions.reason: Their messages are kept in the books of Haggai and Zechariah. Both are dated to the second year of King Darius (Haggai 1:1; Zechariah 1:1), about 520 BC, the year named in 4:24. Haggai rebuked the people for living in finished houses while God's house lay in ruins (Haggai 1:4); Zechariah encouraged Zerubbabel that the work would be finished (Zechariah 4:9).

decisions.choice: son of Iddo: of the family of Iddo
decisions.reason: Zechariah 1:1 calls him son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, and Nehemiah 12:16 lists a priestly family of Iddo. Here, as in 6:14, "son" names him by his better-known forebear, as Hebrew and Aramaic often do.

decisions.choice: over them: the God of Israel who was over the people
alternatives: the name that was over them
decisions.reason: The phrase most naturally describes God as the one over the Jews, their Lord and protector. It may also mean that his name was called over them, marking them as his people (compare Jeremiah 14:9). Both readings say the same thing in the end: the prophets spoke with the authority of the God to whom Judah belonged.

decisions.choice: spoke God's messages; who ruled over his people
decisions.reason: Readable says what prophesying is and makes the people explicit as the ones God was over (m3).

records.heading: Work on the house of God begins again

records.source: בֵּאדַ֡יִן קָ֠מוּ זְרֻבָּבֶ֤ל בַּר־שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל֙ וְיֵשׁ֣וּעַ בַּר־יֽוֹצָדָ֔ק וְשָׁרִ֣יו לְמִבְנֵ֔א בֵּ֥ית אֱלָהָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירֽוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וְעִמְּה֛וֹן נְבִיַּיָּ֥א דִֽי־אֱלָהָ֖א מְסָעֲדִ֥ין לְהֽוֹן׃פ
records.gloss: Then arose Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak and began to build [the] house of God which [is] in Jerusalem; and with them [were] the prophets of God, supporting them.
pieces: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak set to work and began again to build the house of God in Jerusalem. The prophets of God were with them, helping them.

L.2: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began to build the house of God which is in Jerusalem, and with them were the prophets of God, supporting them.

R.2: So Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak started again to build God's temple in Jerusalem. God's prophets were with them and helped them.

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel and Jeshua: the governor and the high priest
decisions.reason: Zerubbabel, of David's royal line, and Jeshua the high priest led the first return and laid the foundation (3:2, 8-10). Haggai addresses them by name and calls Zerubbabel governor of Judah (Haggai 1:1, 14).

decisions.choice: arose and began to build: work resumed after it had stopped
decisions.reason: The foundation had been laid years earlier (3:10), but the work stopped under pressure from the peoples around (4:4-5, 24). "Arose" marks a fresh start, which is why Balanced says "began again".

decisions.choice: supporting them: helping, perhaps with their words and their hands
decisions.reason: The verb means to support or sustain. It may mean the encouragement of their prophecies (verse 1; Haggai 2:4) or that they also took part in the work; the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: began again (B); started again (R)
decisions.reason: "Again" is supplied because the work had begun before and been stopped (m2).

records.source: בֵּהּ־זִמְנָא֩ אֲתָ֨א עֲלֵיה֜וֹן תַּ֠תְּנַי פַּחַ֧ת עֲבַֽר־נַהֲרָ֛ה וּשְׁתַ֥ר בּוֹזְנַ֖י וּכְנָוָתְה֑וֹן וְכֵן֙ אָמְרִ֣ין לְהֹ֔ם מַן־שָׂ֨ם לְכֹ֜ם טְעֵ֗ם בַּיְתָ֤א דְנָה֙ לִבְּנֵ֔א וְאֻשַּׁרְנָ֥א דְנָ֖ה לְשַׁכְלָלָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: At it, the time, came to them Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues, and thus [they were] saying to them: Who made for you a decree this house to build and this structure to finish?
pieces: At that time Tattenai, the governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues came to them and asked, "Who gave you an order to build this house and to finish this structure?"

L.3: At that time Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues came to them and said thus to them: "Who issued you a decree to build this house and to finish this structure?"

R.3: At that time Tattenai, the governor of the province west of the Euphrates River, came to them with Shethar-bozenai and the other officials. They asked, "Who gave you permission to build this temple and finish it?"

decisions.choice: Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River: the Persian governor of the lands west of the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "Beyond the River" was the Persian name for the province west of the Euphrates, seen from the Persian heartland: Syria, Phoenicia, Samaria and Judah. A governor named Tattenai of this province is known from a Babylonian document of Darius's reign. He was over the local governors such as Zerubbabel.

decisions.choice: a decree: an official order with royal authority
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word means a command or decision. The question is whether the building has the king's authority behind it, since unlicensed building in a subject province could be taken as rebellion (compare 4:12-16).

decisions.choice: this structure: a word of uncertain meaning
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word is rare (also verse 9) and probably borrowed from Persian. It may mean the building's structure as a whole, its walls, or its timber work and fittings. In context it stands beside "this house" and means the work going on at the temple.

decisions.choice: the province west of the Euphrates River
decisions.reason: Readable says where "Beyond the River" was, as the book-wide choice for Ezra does.

records.source: אֱדַ֥יִן כְּנֵ֖מָא אֲמַ֣רְנָא לְּהֹ֑ם מַן־אִנּוּן֙ שְׁמָהָ֣ת גֻּבְרַיָּ֔א דִּֽי־דְנָ֥ה בִנְיָנָ֖א בָּנַֽיִן׃
records.gloss: Then thus we said to them: What [are] they, [the] names of the men who this building [are] building?
pieces: We also asked them, "What are the names of the men who are putting up this building?"

L.4: Then we said to them thus: "What are the names of the men who are building this building?"

R.4: We also asked them for the names of the men who were doing the building.

decisions.choice: we said: the received text has the first person; old Greek and Syriac read "they said"
decisions.reason: In the Masoretic text the verse slips into "we", as if the officials' report (verses 8-10, "we went", "we asked") were already being quoted. The Greek and Syriac translations have "they said", which continues the narrative of verse 3 with a second question. The Hebrew text governs here; the sense is the same either way: the officials asked for the builders' names (verse 10).

decisions.choice: what are the names: a second question from the officials
alternatives: the Jews told the officials what the names were
decisions.reason: Read with "we", the clause could also be the Jews' reply, with the narrator speaking for them. But verse 10 says the officials asked for the leaders' names in order to write them down, so the clause is best read as the officials' question.

decisions.choice: asked them for the names
decisions.reason: Readable turns the quoted question into a statement; the sense is the same.

records.source: וְעֵ֣ין אֱלָהֲהֹ֗ם הֲוָת֙ עַל־שָׂבֵ֣י יְהוּדָיֵ֔א וְלָא־בַטִּ֣לוּ הִמּ֔וֹ עַד־טַעְמָ֖א לְדָרְיָ֣וֶשׁ יְהָ֑ךְ וֶאֱדַ֛יִן יְתִיב֥וּן נִשְׁתְּוָנָ֖א עַל־דְּנָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And [the] eye of their God was on [the] elders of the Jews, and not they made cease them until [the] report to Darius should go and then they should return a letter concerning this.
pieces: But the eye of their God was watching over the elders of the Jews, and the officials did not stop them until a report could reach Darius and a written answer about it could come back.

L.5: But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they did not stop them until a report should go to Darius and then a letter should be returned concerning it.

R.5: But God was watching over the leaders of the Jews. So the officials did not stop the work while a report was sent to King Darius and they waited for his answer.

decisions.choice: the eye of their God was on them: God watched over them with care
decisions.reason: God's eye on someone means his attention and protection (Psalm 33:18; Ezra 7:6, 28 says the same with God's hand). The writer sees God's care behind the officials' decision to let the work go on.

decisions.choice: Darius: Darius I, king of Persia 522-486 BC
decisions.reason: This is Darius son of Hystaspes, who took the throne in 522 BC after a time of revolt. His second year (4:24; Haggai 1:1) was 520 BC. He organized the empire into provinces with governors and royal records, which fits the search of the archives in 6:1-2.

decisions.choice: they did not stop them: the officials let the building continue while they waited
decisions.reason: The subject is Tattenai and his colleagues, and "them" is the elders. The officials could have halted the work at once; instead they wrote to the king and let it go on.

decisions.choice: the officials
decisions.reason: Balanced names the subject, which the Aramaic leaves as "they" (m3).

decisions.choice: God was watching over the leaders
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of God's eye (m1) and says "leaders" for elders, the heads of the families who led the community.

records.source: פַּרְשֶׁ֣גֶן אִ֠גַּרְתָּא דִּֽי־שְׁלַ֞ח תַּתְּנַ֣י׀פַּחַ֣ת עֲבַֽר־נַהֲרָ֗ה וּשְׁתַ֤ר בּוֹזְנַי֙ וּכְנָ֣וָתֵ֔הּ אֲפַ֨רְסְכָיֵ֔א דִּ֖י בַּעֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָ֑ה עַל־דָּרְיָ֖וֶשׁ מַלְכָּֽא׃
records.gloss: [The] copy of the letter which sent Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and his colleagues, the officials who [were] in Beyond the River, to Darius the king.
pieces: This is a copy of the letter that Tattenai the governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues, the officials in the province Beyond the River, sent to King Darius.

L.6: The copy of the letter that Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and his colleagues, the officials who were in Beyond the River, sent to Darius the king.

R.6: Here is a copy of the letter that Tattenai the governor, Shethar-bozenai and the other officials of the province west of the Euphrates sent to King Darius.

decisions.choice: the officials: a Persian word of uncertain meaning
decisions.reason: The word is borrowed from Persian and occurs also in 6:6 (and a similar one in 4:9). Older translations took it as the name of a people. It is now usually understood as a title for a kind of official, perhaps an inspector or envoy. Here it describes Tattenai's colleagues.

decisions.choice: the copy of the letter: the writer quotes the official record
decisions.reason: Ezra 4-7 quotes several royal letters in Aramaic, the language used for government letters across the Persian empire (4:7, 11; 7:11). "Copy" is a Persian loanword for a written copy of a document.

decisions.choice: This is (B); Here is (R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic is a heading, "The copy of the letter"; Balanced and Readable make it a sentence.

records.heading: Tattenai's letter to King Darius

records.source: פִּתְגָמָ֖א שְׁלַ֣חוּ עֲל֑וֹהִי וְכִדְנָה֙ כְּתִ֣יב בְּגַוֵּ֔הּ לְדָרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֖א שְׁלָמָ֥א כֹֽלָּא׃ס
records.gloss: The report they sent to him, and thus [it was] written in it: To Darius the king, all peace.
pieces: The report they sent him read as follows: "To King Darius: All peace.

L.7: They sent a report to him, and thus it was written in it: "To Darius the king, all peace.

R.7: This is what their report said: "To King Darius. We wish you peace and well-being.

decisions.choice: all peace: the greeting of a letter
decisions.reason: A letter of the time began with the name of the one it was sent to and a wish for his peace, that is, his welfare. "Peace" here is the opening greeting, as in other Aramaic letters (4:17; 7:12). The letter runs to the end of verse 17.

decisions.choice: We wish you peace and well-being
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the greeting, keeping "peace" and adding what it meant in a greeting (m1).

records.source: יְדִ֣יעַ׀לֶהֱוֵ֣א לְמַלְכָּ֗א דִּֽי־אֲזַ֜לְנָא לִיה֤וּד מְדִֽינְתָּא֙ לְבֵית֙ אֱלָהָ֣א רַבָּ֔א וְה֤וּא מִתְבְּנֵא֙ אֶ֣בֶן גְּלָ֔ל וְאָ֖ע מִתְּשָׂ֣ם בְּכֻתְלַיָּ֑א וַעֲבִ֥ידְתָּא דָ֛ךְ אָסְפַּ֥רְנָא מִתְעַבְדָ֖א וּמַצְלַ֥ח בְּיֶדְהֹֽם׃ס
records.gloss: Known let it be to the king that we went to Judah the province to [the] house of the great God, and it [is] being built [with] stones of rolling, and timber [is] being set in the walls, and this work diligently [is] being done and prospers in their hand.
pieces: Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. It is being built with large stones, and timbers are being laid in the walls. The work is being carried out diligently and is making good progress in their hands.

L.8: Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God, and it is being built with huge stones, and timber is being set in the walls; and this work is being done diligently and is prospering in their hand.

R.8: Your Majesty should know that we went to the province of Judah, to the temple of the great God. The people are building it with huge stones and putting beams into the walls. They are working hard, and the work is going well.

decisions.choice: stones of rolling: very large stones, too heavy to carry
decisions.reason: The phrase means stones that had to be rolled into place (also 6:4), that is, large blocks. It may also mean cut and finished stone. Either way the officials report that this is solid, serious building, not a makeshift shrine.

decisions.choice: timber set in the walls: courses of wood laid between courses of stone
decisions.reason: Building with layers of beams between rows of stone was used for strength (1 Kings 6:36; 7:12; compare Ezra 6:4). The officials describe the method they saw.

decisions.choice: the great God: the officials' own respectful words
decisions.reason: The Persian officials call the God of the Jews "the great God", using the title the Jews themselves used (verse 11). It is the language of an official report, not a confession of their own faith.

decisions.choice: diligently: with care and with speed
decisions.reason: The Persian loanword means exactly, carefully, or promptly. It appears again in Darius's reply (6:8, 12, 13), where the king orders that his decree be carried out with the same care.

decisions.choice: Your Majesty should know
decisions.reason: Readable puts the formal opening "Let it be known to the king" in plain terms of address.

records.source: אֱדַ֗יִן שְׁאֵ֨לְנָא֙ לְשָׂבַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֔ךְ כְּנֵ֖מָא אֲמַ֣רְנָא לְּהֹ֑םמַן־שָׂ֨ם לְכֹ֜ם טְעֵ֗ם בַּיְתָ֤א דְנָה֙ לְמִבְנְיָ֔ה וְאֻשַּׁרְנָ֥א דְנָ֖ה לְשַׁכְלָלָֽה׃
records.gloss: Then we asked those elders; thus we said to them: Who made for you a decree this house to build and this structure to finish?
pieces: We asked those elders, "Who gave you an order to build this house and to finish this structure?"

L.9: Then we asked those elders; thus we said to them: "Who issued you a decree to build this house and to finish this structure?"

R.9: We asked their leaders, "Who gave you permission to build this temple and finish it?"

decisions.choice: this structure: as in verse 3
decisions.reason: The officials repeat the question of verse 3 word for word; the rare word is discussed there.

decisions.choice: permission
decisions.reason: Readable says "permission" because the officials wanted to know whether the king had authorized the work (verse 3).

records.source: וְאַ֧ף שְׁמָהָתְהֹ֛ם שְׁאֵ֥לְנָא לְּהֹ֖םלְהוֹדָעוּתָ֑ךְ דִּ֛י נִכְתֻּ֥ב שֻׁם־גֻּבְרַיָּ֖א דִּ֥י בְרָאשֵׁיהֹֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And also their names we asked them, to make known to you, that we might write [the] name[s] of the men who [are] at their heads.
pieces: We also asked them their names, so that we could inform you by writing down the names of the men who are their leaders.

L.10: And we also asked them their names, to make them known to you, so that we might write down the names of the men who are at their head.

R.10: We also asked for the names of their leaders, so that we could write them down and send them to you.

decisions.choice: to write the names of the leaders: the men answerable to the king
decisions.reason: A list of names told the king who was responsible for the work. If the building proved unlawful, those named could be held to account; if it was lawful, the king knew whom his orders concerned.

decisions.choice: so that we could inform you by writing down (B); write them down and send them to you (R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic gives two purposes side by side, to inform the king and to write the names; Balanced and Readable join them so the order of events is clear.

records.source: וּכְנֵ֥מָא פִתְגָמָ֖א הֲתִיב֣וּנָא לְמֵמַ֑ר אֲנַ֣חְנָא הִמּ֡וֹ עַבְדוֹהִי֩ דִֽי־אֱלָ֨הּ שְׁמַיָּ֜א וְאַרְעָ֗א וּבָנַ֤יִן בַּיְתָא֙ דִּֽי־הֲוָ֨א בְנֵ֜ה מִקַּדְמַ֤ת דְּנָה֙ שְׁנִ֣ין שַׂגִּיאָ֔ן וּמֶ֤לֶךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ רַ֔ב בְּנָ֖הִי וְשַׁכְלְלֵֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And thus [the] word they returned to us, saying: We, we [are] servants of the God of the heavens and the earth, and [we are] building the house that was built from before this many years, and a great king of Israel built it and finished it.
pieces: This is the answer they gave us: 'We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the house that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and completed.

L.11: And thus they returned word to us, saying, 'We are the slaves of the God of heaven and earth, and we are building the house that was built many years before this, which a great king of Israel built and finished.

R.11: This is how they answered us: 'We serve the God of heaven and earth. We are rebuilding the temple that was first built many years ago. A great king of Israel built it and finished it.

decisions.choice: his servants: those who belong to God and work for him
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word is the same as the Hebrew word for a slave or servant: one who belongs to a master, not a hired worker. The elders answer the king's officials by naming the master they serve, the God of heaven and earth, whose authority stands above any earthly ruler.

decisions.choice: the God of heaven and earth: the creator who rules over all
decisions.reason: The elders do not speak of a local god of Judah but of the God who made heaven and earth. "The God of heaven" is the title used for Israel's God in the Persian documents of Ezra (1:2; 6:9-10; 7:12, 21).

decisions.choice: a great king of Israel: Solomon
decisions.reason: Solomon built the first temple about 960 BC (1 Kings 6:1, 37-38). The elders point out that the house is no new venture but the restoration of an ancient one, which would matter to a Persian king who respected old sanctuaries.

decisions.choice: servants (B); We serve (R)
decisions.reason: Following the project's rule, Literal says "slaves" and Balanced and Readable "servants"; the meaning decision keeps the sense of belonging to a master.

decisions.choice: rebuilding
decisions.reason: "Building" a house that had stood before means rebuilding it; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: לָהֵ֗ן מִן־דִּ֨י הַרְגִּ֤זוּ אֲבָהֳתַ֨נָא֙ לֶאֱלָ֣הּ שְׁמַיָּ֔א יְהַ֣ב הִמּ֔וֹ בְּיַ֛ד נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל כַּסְדָּאָ֑ה וּבַיְתָ֤ה דְנָה֙ סַתְרֵ֔הּ וְעַמָּ֖ה הַגְלִ֥י לְבָבֶֽל׃ס
records.gloss: But because our fathers angered the God of the heavens, he gave them into [the] hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, and this house he destroyed and the people he exiled to Babylon.
pieces: But because our ancestors made the God of heaven angry, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house and took the people into exile in Babylon.

L.12: But because our fathers angered the God of heaven, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house and carried the people away into exile to Babylon.

R.12: But our ancestors made the God of heaven angry. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let Nebuchadnezzar, the Chaldean king of Babylon, defeat them. Nebuchadnezzar destroyed this temple and took the people away as captives to Babylon.

decisions.choice: because our fathers angered God, he gave them over: the exile was God's judgment
decisions.reason: The elders admit that the temple was not lost because their God was weak but because he gave his people over for their sin, as the prophets had warned (2 Kings 24:3-4; 2 Chronicles 36:15-17). The same God now allows its rebuilding.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar the Chaldean: the king of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem in 587/586 BC
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar II ruled Babylon 605-562 BC. The Chaldeans were the people from southern Mesopotamia whose dynasty ruled Babylon in his time. His army burned the temple (2 Kings 25:8-9).

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the earlier generations, men and women; Balanced and Readable say "ancestors".

decisions.choice: let Nebuchadnezzar defeat them
decisions.reason: Readable explains "gave them into the hand", an idiom for handing someone over to an enemy's power.

records.source: בְּרַם֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת חֲדָ֔ה לְכ֥וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֖א דִּ֣י בָבֶ֑ל כּ֤וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּא֙ שָׂ֣ם טְעֵ֔ם בֵּית־אֱלָהָ֥א דְנָ֖ה לִבְּנֵֽא׃
records.gloss: Nevertheless, in year one of Cyrus king of Babylon, Cyrus the king made a decree this house of God to build.
pieces: However, in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued a decree that this house of God should be rebuilt.

L.13: However, in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, Cyrus the king issued a decree to build this house of God.

R.13: But in the first year that Cyrus was king of Babylon, he gave an order that this temple of God should be built again.

decisions.choice: the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon: 539/538 BC
decisions.reason: Cyrus the Persian took Babylon in 539 BC; his first year as its king began in 538 BC. The decree is the one recorded in 1:1-4. The elders call him king of Babylon, the title that mattered for the land Babylon had ruled.

decisions.choice: rebuilt (B); built again (R)
decisions.reason: The decree was to build the house again on its old site; Balanced and Readable say so, as in verse 11.

records.source: וְ֠אַף מָאנַיָּ֣א דִֽי־בֵית־אֱלָהָא֮ דִּ֣י דַהֲבָ֣ה וְכַסְפָּא֒ דִּ֣י נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר הַנְפֵּק֙ מִן־הֵֽיכְלָא֙ דִּ֣י בִֽירוּשְׁלֶ֔ם וְהֵיבֵ֣ל הִמּ֔וֹ לְהֵיכְלָ֖א דִּ֣י בָבֶ֑ל הַנְפֵּ֨ק הִמּ֜וֹ כּ֣וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֗א מִן־הֵֽיכְלָא֙ דִּ֣י בָבֶ֔ל וִיהִ֨יבוּ֙ לְשֵׁשְׁבַּצַּ֣ר שְׁמֵ֔הּ דִּ֥י פֶחָ֖ה שָׂמֵֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And also the vessels of the house of God of gold and silver which Nebuchadnezzar brought out from the temple which [was] in Jerusalem and carried them to the temple of Babylon, these brought out Cyrus the king from the temple of Babylon, and they were given to [one], Sheshbazzar [was] his name, whom he had made governor.
pieces: King Cyrus also took out of the temple in Babylon the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to the temple in Babylon. He handed them over to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor.

L.14: And also the vessels of gold and silver of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple that was in Jerusalem and brought to the temple of Babylon, these Cyrus the king brought out from the temple of Babylon, and they were given to one whose name was Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor.

R.14: Nebuchadnezzar had taken the gold and silver bowls and other objects from God's temple in Jerusalem and put them in the temple in Babylon. But King Cyrus took them out of that temple and gave them to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor.

decisions.choice: the temple of Babylon: the shrine of Babylon's god
decisions.reason: Conquerors placed the sacred objects of defeated peoples in the temple of their own god as trophies (compare 1 Samuel 5:2; Daniel 1:2). Returning them was a public act: it showed that Cyrus restored the worship of the gods of conquered peoples, and for Israel it fulfilled God's promise (1:7-11; Jeremiah 27:21-22).

decisions.choice: Sheshbazzar the governor: the leader of the first return
decisions.reason: Sheshbazzar is called "the prince of Judah" in 1:8 and received the vessels then (1:7-11). Here Cyrus is said to have made him governor. How he relates to Zerubbabel, who led the people at the same time (2:2; 3:8), the text does not say.

decisions.choice: vessels: the temple's sacred utensils
decisions.reason: The word covers all kinds of containers and implements used in worship; 1:9-10 lists basins, bowls and knives.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar had taken ... But King Cyrus took them out
decisions.reason: Readable tells the events in the order they happened, in two sentences.

records.source: וַאֲמַר־לֵ֓הּ׀אֵ֚ל מָֽאנַיָּ֔א שֵׂ֚א אֵֽזֶל־אֲחֵ֣ת הִמּ֔וֹ בְּהֵיכְלָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וּבֵ֥ית אֱלָהָ֖א יִתְבְּנֵ֥א עַל־אַתְרֵֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: And he said to him: These vessels take, go, deposit them in the temple which [is] in Jerusalem, and [the] house of God let it be built on its place.
pieces: Cyrus told him, "Take these vessels, go and put them in the temple in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt on its original site."

L.15: And he said to him, "Take these vessels; go, deposit them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be built on its place."

R.15: Cyrus told him, "Take these objects and go. Put them in the temple in Jerusalem, and rebuild God's temple where it stood before."

decisions.choice: on its place: on the same site as before
decisions.reason: The house was to stand where Solomon's temple had stood (also 2:68; 6:7). The site itself was holy, which is why the returned exiles built the altar "on its foundations" (3:3).

decisions.choice: Cyrus told him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, who is the "he" of the Aramaic.

records.source: אֱדַ֨יִן֙ שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּ֣ר דֵּ֔ךְ אֲתָ֗א יְהַ֧ב אֻשַּׁיָּ֛א דִּי־בֵ֥ית אֱלָהָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וּמִן־אֱדַ֧יִן וְעַד־כְּעַ֛ן מִתְבְּנֵ֖א וְלָ֥א שְׁלִֽם׃
records.gloss: Then this Sheshbazzar came, he laid the foundations of the house of God which [is] in Jerusalem, and from then and until now [it is] being built and not [is it] finished.
pieces: So this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem. From that time until now it has been under construction, and it is still not finished.'

L.16: Then this Sheshbazzar came [and] laid the foundations of the house of God that is in Jerusalem, and from then until now it has been under construction and is not finished.'

R.16: So Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of God's temple in Jerusalem. It has been under construction from that time until now, but it is not finished yet.'

decisions.choice: Sheshbazzar laid the foundations: he led the work that 3:8-10 describes
decisions.reason: Chapter 3 tells of Zerubbabel and Jeshua leading the laying of the foundation. The elders credit it to Sheshbazzar, the governor appointed by Cyrus, whose name carried weight with the Persian court. He may have begun the work under his authority while Zerubbabel led it on site, or the two names may belong to the same period of leadership seen from two sides; the text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: from then until now it is being built and is not finished: the work has never been completed
decisions.reason: The elders present the work as one continuous project begun under Cyrus's decree, so that it needed no new permission. They pass over the years when it stood still (4:24).

records.source: וּכְעַ֞ן הֵ֧ן עַל־מַלְכָּ֣א טָ֗ב יִ֠תְבַּקַּר בְּבֵ֨ית גִּנְזַיָּ֜א דִּי־מַלְכָּ֣א תַמָּה֮ דִּ֣י בְּבָבֶל֒ הֵ֣ן אִיתַ֗י דִּֽי־מִן־כּ֤וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּא֙ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵ֔ם לְמִבְנֵ֛א בֵּית־אֱלָהָ֥א דֵ֖ךְ בִּירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וּרְע֥וּת מַלְכָּ֛א עַל־דְּנָ֖ה יִשְׁלַ֥ח עֲלֶֽינָא׃ס
records.gloss: And now, if to the king [it is] good, let it be searched in the house of the treasures of the king there which [is] in Babylon, whether there is [that] from Cyrus the king a decree was made to build this house of God in Jerusalem; and the will of the king concerning this let him send to us.
pieces: Now, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the royal archives in Babylon to see whether King Cyrus really issued a decree to rebuild this house of God in Jerusalem. Then let the king send us his decision on this matter."

L.17: And now, if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the king's treasure house there in Babylon, whether it is so that a decree was issued by Cyrus the king to build this house of God in Jerusalem; and let the king send us his will concerning this."

R.17: Now, if Your Majesty agrees, please have someone search the royal records in Babylon. See whether King Cyrus really gave an order to rebuild this temple of God in Jerusalem. Then please tell us what you want us to do about this."

decisions.choice: the king's treasure house: the royal archive where documents were kept
decisions.reason: Royal treasuries also stored official records. 6:1 calls it "the house of the scrolls" where the treasures were kept, and the scroll was finally found at Ecbatana (6:2).

decisions.choice: whether it is so: the officials neither deny nor accept the claim
decisions.reason: Tattenai does not accuse the Jews of lying; he asks the king to check. The question is left open for the king to decide, and the reply in chapter 6 settles it.

decisions.choice: his decision
decisions.reason: The king's "will" in a letter like this is his ruling on the case.

decisions.choice: if Your Majesty agrees, please
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the polite address of an official letter in plain words.
